content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates in the middle to late horizon when prices are trending downward or consolidating.
- Shows persistent lag in reacting to recent price drops — forecasts remain too high longer than actuals.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., post-90+ spikes), then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to overcorrect toward historical averages, missing short-term volatility.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early values and underestimate late values, suggesting asymmetric error structure.
- Avoids sharp downward corrections after high peaks — model holds too much upward momentum too long.
